items.quote: In numeris $8k+1$ semper $2n$[-$-1$-] [-Classes q-] multiplicatores seu Classes quae constituunt $4n$ indices ... in numeris $8k+5$ $2n$ classes, quae praebent $4n-2$ indices: ast in numeris $8K+3$. $6n-3$ indices ex quibus fiunt $3n-1$ Classes
items.english: For numbers 8k+1 there are always 2n multipliers or classes, which make up 4n indices ... for numbers 8k+5, 2n classes, which give 4n−2 indices; but for numbers 8k+3, 6n−3 indices, from which 3n−1 classes arise.

items.quote: quaternarius hic semper indices $2n-1$; $4n-2$ adipiscitur: ita ut si quadrati fracti denominatore 4 admittantur, terni indices ternaeque classes coincidant atque sic illorum numerus in $2n-1$, harum in $n$ abeant. ($n$ = num. discerptt. divers. in 3 $\square$)
items.english: Here the number 4 always obtains the indices 2n−1; 4n−2: so that if squares of fractions with denominator 4 are admitted, indices coincide in threes and classes in threes, and thus the number of the former becomes 2n−1, that of the latter n. (n = number of different decompositions into 3 squares)
